summary: STEP 2 persistence + Free/Pro entitlement testing of CarryCue (Expo web preview, 390x844 mobile viewport, frontend-only, no backend involved). Tested via Playwright against https://carry-preview.preview.emergentagent.com. ALL 12 requested scenarios PASSED with no bugs found: (1) Item persistence across full page reload verified (added 'Passport', reloaded, still present). (2) Completed-item toggle state persists across reload (Wallet checked, survived reload, correctly sorted to bottom). (3) Duplicate prevention works case/whitespace-insensitively ('  wallet  ' -> 'Already on your list', count stayed at 1, held after reload). (4) Forgot Something flow: added 'Notebook', 'Saved' screen shown, item appeared on Home list and persisted after reload. (5) Frequently Used: home chips and Quick Add sheet chips are byte-identical, ordering changes correctly based on real usage/forgotten stats (Notebook jumped to #1 after forgot-flow boost), max 5 shown, no scores displayed. (6) Routines persistence: renamed 'Everyday'->'Everyday Renamed', added 'Sunglasses' item, both survived reload; deleted 'School' routine via trash icon, stayed deleted after reload. (7) FREE item limit: could add up to exactly 5 active items; 6th attempt correctly blocked with 'Remember more with CarryCue Pro' upgrade sheet, item NOT added (count stayed 5). (8) PRO removes item limit: 6th+ item added successfully, no upgrade prompt. (9) FREE custom routine limit: 1st custom routine succeeded (navigated to detail), 2nd attempt correctly blocked with 'Create unlimited routines with CarryCue Pro' sheet, no 2nd routine created. (10) PRO allows multiple routines: additional custom routine created with no prompt. (11) Downgrade PRO->FREE preserves all existing data (routine/item counts unchanged) and re-blocks further additions over the Free limit via upgrade sheet (does not silently fail or delete). (12) Regression: Quick Add sheet open/close via backdrop works, 'Choose time or place' correctly navigates to /trigger, 'Use this routine' adds non-duplicate items under PRO and is properly blocked by the same upgrade sheet under FREE when it would exceed the 5-item cap (verified this is correct capacity-based behavior, not a bug).
critical_code_review_comments: repository.ts / store.tsx: clean separation of concerns, dedupeByName() heals any legacy duplicate data on every load — good defensive design.
limits.ts + UPGRADE_COPY centralizes Free/Pro copy and limits well; addItem/newRoutine/addLocation all follow the same AddResult/CreateRoutineResult pattern consistently.

frequentlyUsed.ts computeFrequentlyUsed is deterministic and shared by both Home and QuickAddSheet via the single `frequentlyUsed` value from useStore() — matches the 'same computed list' requirement exactly, no separate hardcoded list found anywhere.

Minor UX note (not a bug): applying a routine while already near the Free 5-item cap can immediately trigger the upgrade sheet if the routine's items would push the total over 5 — this is correct/intended per the capacity logic in applyRoutine(), just worth knowing when manually testing 'Use this routine' on Free.

Playwright automation note: BottomSheet's fixed-position overlay causes Playwright's actionability check ('scrolling into view') to report elements 'outside of the viewport' even when visibly on-screen; using page.evaluate()-based JS clicks (bypassing Playwright's viewport check) was required as a workaround for buttons inside the sheet (quick-add-save, dev-reset-data, etc.). This is a testing-tool quirk of the position:fixed approach, not a functional app bug — regular user clicks/taps work fine as shown by console-log-free successful interactions.

seed_data_creation: Used Settings -> Developer tools -> 'Reset local data' before most test runs to guarantee a known fresh seed state (Wallet, Student ID, Charger, Umbrella + 3 seed routines: Everyday, School, Gym).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Note: each separate browser_automation tool invocation appears to start with fresh localStorage/browser context (no persistence carried over BETWEEN tool calls) — persistence must be verified via page.reload() WITHIN the same script call, which is what was done here. Dev tools testIDs used: settings-button, dev-tools-section, dev-set-free, dev-set-pro, dev-reset-data. Upgrade sheet testIDs: upgrade-sheet, upgrade-sheet-upgrade, upgrade-sheet-dismiss. All STEP 2 persistence, entitlement/limit, and Frequently-Used-computation requirements are implemented correctly and match the spec exactly. No RevenueCat/real purchases present (as expected, this is a mock foundation only) — flagged as intentionally MOCKED per the review request, not a defect.
